Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
31-year-old man with 5-day history of dry cough, coryza, myalgia, and low-grade systemic symptoms; clinical picture consistent with viral upper respiratory tract infection.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry, hacking cough and runny nose for ~5 days, beginning at start of last weekend.  
• Associated symptoms: Muscle aches, occasional headache, chills. Denies dyspnea, wheeze, chest tightness, hemoptysis, or purulent sputum.  
• Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (≈5–6 yrs), hypertension.  
• Medications: Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented; Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol as needed – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Self-monitoring: Home blood glucose and BP reportedly within normal range.  
• Allergies: Not documented.  
• Social / preventive: Not discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Oropharynx: Mild posterior pharyngeal erythema; tonsils not enlarged.  
• Neck: No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy (patient report).  
• Chest: Not formally examined; patient denies wheeze/shortness of breath.

Impression:
Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection.

Plan:
• Symptomatic relief with over-the-counter combination products (e.g., Day Nurse/Night Nurse) deemed compatible with current medications.  
• Return/seek care if:
  – Development of shortness of breath, wheeze, or other respiratory compromise.  
  – Symptoms persist beyond ≈3 weeks or clinically worsen.  
• No prescription or further investigation required at present.

Quality checks:

● Missing but expected: Allergy status, smoking status, alcohol intake, vaccination status, exact medication doses, formal vitals.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript generally clear; minor conversational fillers present but did not impede data extraction.
